name: Eriksen Estring
question: Does an estradiol-releasing vaginal ring delay recurrent urinary tract infection in postmenopausal women?

design.population: Postmenopausal women with recurrent symptomatic, bacteriologically confirmed urinary tract infections.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Study design and Results

verdictNote: Time to first recurrence favored the ring; the comparator received no estrogen.
takeaway: In postmenopausal women with recurrent urinary tract infection, the estradiol-releasing vaginal ring Estring prolonged time to first recurrence versus no estrogen treatment; estimated infection-free survival at 36 weeks was approximately 45% versus 20% (log-rank P = 0.008).

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Eriksen B. "A randomized, open, parallel-group study on the preventive effect of an estradiol-releasing vaginal ring (Estring) on recurrent urinary tract infections in postmenopausal women." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 1999;180(5):1072-1079. doi:10.1016/S0002-9378(99)70597-1
reports.followUp: 36 weeks of ring treatment; controls followed for 36 weeks or until first recurrence

results.measure: Kaplan–Meier estimate of remaining free of UTI at 36 weeks
results.note: Log-rank comparison of time to first recurrence; estimates are not crude event proportions.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Study design and Results

results.measure: Vaginal pH decrease and vaginal and urethral cell maturation

values.exp: Lower vaginal pH; more mature vaginal and, to a lesser extent, urethral mucosal cells

results.note: The abstract gives no arm-specific values or effect estimates.

harms.label: Unexpected adverse events
harms.note: The report abstract states that no unexpected adverse events were found.

delivery.label: Ring regimen
delivery.value: Estring contained 2 mg estradiol; each ring was carried vaginally for 12 weeks during a 36-week treatment period.

relations.note: Both found fewer recurrences with vaginal estrogen; Eriksen tested an estradiol ring against no estrogen treatment.
